text:
If you were waiting for Monday to brighten up, it hasn’t happened yet. Burlington is sitting under a gray sky at 61, with a damp feel and barely any breeze, and the afternoon looks more like a continuation than a turnaround. Showers should come in rounds through the rest of the day and into the evening, with temperatures stuck near the low 60s. The forecast models disagree on just how wet we get, but the wetter side has my attention, so keep the umbrella handy. On the lake, north winds and 1 to 2 foot waves make for a choppy afternoon, building a bit tonight.

Tuesday is the reset, with some morning cloudiness giving way to breaks of sun and a high near 65. Winds stay manageable, and the lake should calm late in the day. Plan on a wet, jacket-worthy Monday evening, then save the longer walk or waterfront time for Tuesday afternoon.

week.blurb: A wet, chilly Monday, with showers likely and a high near 62; keep daytime plans flexible.
Partly sunny, fairly quiet Tuesday, with a high near 65 and a comfortable night ahead.
Partly sunny and milder Wednesday, reaching near 72, with a dry stretch for daytime plans.
A partly sunny, breezy Thursday climbs near 77, a good day for outdoor plans before showers may develop at night.
Friday turns cooler, near 70, with a chance of showers, so carry a rain jacket.
Mostly sunny and cool Saturday, near 64, with a dry-looking day for outdoor plans.
Sunday stays near 64 with sun and a chance of showers, so keep plans flexible.
